correctness.rationale: Positive diagonal scaling and a sign change give r∈(0,1), q=1−β and s=βr for both directions. Current/current has eigenvalues q±s. One-stale on (u_k,v_k,v_{k−1}) has characteristic z(z−q)^2−s²: when q∈[0,1), |z|≥1 would imply |z||z−q|²≥β²>s². When β>1, put d=β−1. The polynomial z(z+d)^2−s² is negative for z≤0 and strictly increasing for z>0, with its positive root p<1 by evaluation at 1. The other roots are a conjugate pair of modulus p+d, by Vieta and p(p+d)^2=s². For 1<β<2, p+d<1 iff the polynomial is positive at 2−β, i.e. 2−β−β²r²>0, giving 4/(1+√(1+8r²)); β≥2 cannot be stable. The pair has unit modulus on the boundary. In stale/stale, the sum and difference quadratics are z²−qz±s. For β<2/(1+r), |s|<1 and both quadratics are positive at ±1, which are the real quadratic Schur conditions. At or above that β, the difference polynomial at −1 is nonpositive, so it has a root at or below −1. Arbitrary real initial histories permit real nondecaying modes whenever a spectral radius is at least one. Swapping the stale direction permutes variables. Strict gain follows from √(1+8r²)<1+2r; the square identity 81(1+8r²)−(7+16r)^2=8(7r−2)^2 gives the 9/8 bound and the sole equality at r=2/7. The ceilings there bracket β=5/3: 14/9<5/3<7/4. Setting q=0 in the three spectra yields the stated spectral factors at β=1. No finite grid is used to establish a universal statement.
residual_risks: The frozen report's 104 comparisons are recorded, not independently executed. The proof only treats simultaneous commits, the fixed message ages, and exact arithmetic.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The contribution is exact quantification, not existence of asynchronous advantage. The one-stale boundary is a conjugate-pair crossing instead of the difference-mode −1 boundary; the coupling maximization uses their different exact thresholds.

evidence: The present two-coordinate asymmetric age pattern has z(z−q)^2−s²; the prior delayed-process matrix technique and qualitative advantage are explicit in the IPDPS paper.
Exchanging stale directions is equivalent by relabeling. Matching formulas in Resultary 1b8d6aef9d3a and 4c8f7d961672 are from later stochastic scalar delay models.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A similar delay augmentation or quadratic root is not by itself the same deterministic protocol or comparison. No covering equivalence is shown by those passages.

The same-day hit 1b839e7f4866 studies stochastic stale Kaczmarz on an identity system; 9ae0040f2dac is a randomly selected-coordinate Gauss–Seidel second-moment law.

originality.rationale: The synchronized ceiling, the use of delay-state matrices and qualitative asynchronous advantage are prior art. The best supported distinct claim is the exact one-edge simultaneous-round ceiling compared with both zero and two stale directions, together with the maximal 9/8 gain. The inspected prior theorems do not yield that contrast or maximization.
residual_risks: Full-text overlap of the 2025 semi-iterative paper and the 2016 delayed overrelaxation paper is unresolved. The original Moga–Dubois matrix passage was not readable. No positive priority claim rests on those access failures.

value.rationale: For the smallest coupled SPD system, the number and placement of stale edges matter even when the maximum delay and fresh self-read assumptions agree. The theorem separates a true one-edge enlargement from no enlargement with two stale edges, proves its exact best size, and includes an explicit separating β. The β=1 factors prevent a stability-window gain from being misread as equal-parameter speedup. This is a motivated, exact comparison not supplied by an arbitrary-delay sufficient bound.
residual_risks: No implication for changing schedules, larger systems, wall-clock advantages, or an optimal protocol at equal computation cost.
